summary: The design aligns with existing toolkit and browser abstractions, but several safety and lifecycle assumptions are not implemented by current contracts. The highest risks are session persistence, direct generated-tool access, overly broad operation filtering, and asynchronous import completion semantics.

suggestions.title: Make cookie persistence an explicit session-owned contract
suggestions.rationale: `OpenAPIToolkit` calls `HTTPService._request()` without cookies, while `_request()` creates a fresh `httpx.AsyncClient` per call. `HTTPService.cookies` is stored but not consumed there, so a login hook cannot persist `sid` or reliably re-authenticate. Define a shared client/cookie-jar lifecycle, capture `Set-Cookie`, serialize 401 retries, and test concurrent first-use calls.

suggestions.title: Replace tag-plus-string blocklisting with an explicit default-deny operation manifest
suggestions.rationale: The persisted digest shows allowed tags containing ordinary POST/PATCH operations for accounts, contacts, invoice series, documents, and settings. Paths such as account creation, contact creation, `:set-default`, `:schedule`, and `:duplicate` are not all covered by the proposed submit suffixes. Expose only an explicit `(method, path)` allowlist whose entries are classified as READ or DRAFT, and assert every generated operation against it.

suggestions.title: Prevent raw generated tools from bypassing the submit gate
suggestions.rationale: The existing confirmation mechanism marks static toolkit method names through `confirming_tools`; `ToolManager` then checks `routing_meta`. Dynamically attached OpenAPI methods do not receive `OperationKind` or confirmation metadata, while the proposed manual gate only surrounds composite operations. Either keep generated methods private and expose only policy-owned composite tools, or generate and test per-operation `routing_meta` before any HTTP request.

suggestions.title: Define path-default precedence and hide account identifiers from schemas
suggestions.rationale: `OpenAPIToolkit._create_pydantic_schema()` currently makes every path parameter required, and `_build_operation_url()` substitutes only values supplied by the caller. Adding `path_defaults` alone will either still require `accountId` or allow an agent-provided account override. Defaults must be injected before validation, omitted from the public schema, and rejected if supplied by the caller.

suggestions.title: Pin and validate the complete OpenAPI document, not only the compact digest
suggestions.rationale: `hooba-openapi-digest.json` contains summarized `operations` and `schemas`, but no OpenAPI `paths`, `components`, or `servers` document usable by `ResolvingParser`. Loading the remote URL at runtime would reintroduce spec drift. Ship or cache the normalized full document with a verified SHA-256 and fail closed when its version or digest changes.

suggestions.title: Handle multipart, binary, and oneOf payloads outside generic JSON generation
suggestions.rationale: The generator only prioritizes JSON and form-urlencoded bodies; its type conversion does not model `oneOf`, and the request path has no file/multipart handling. The digest includes invoice-line variants, document uploads, and download endpoints, while the toolkit defaults to JSON responses. Use explicit Hooba request models and transport methods for these operations, with multipart and binary replay tests.

suggestions.title: Specify how environment credentials become a broker provider
suggestions.rationale: `CredentialBroker` supports registered resolvers and `static_key`, but its built-in static-key path reads from a vault; it does not map `HOOBA_USERNAME` and `HOOBA_PASSWORD` from the environment. The existing Hooba example bypasses the broker with `navconfig`. Add an explicit bootstrap resolver/registration contract at the application boundary and test missing identity, missing provider, and secret-shape failures before network access.

suggestions.title: Do not depend on document.cookie for REST session transfer
suggestions.rationale: `exec_get_cookies()` explicitly reads `document.cookie`, which cannot see HttpOnly cookies and returns no domain/path metadata. `AbstractDriver` has no cookie API, while `PlaywrightDriver` owns a browser context that can provide complete cookies. Add a driver capability for context-level cookie export/import and fail closed if the authenticated `sid` is unavailable.

suggestions.title: Make bank imports await actual draft completion
suggestions.rationale: `BusinessAutomationToolkit.run_operation()` creates a background task and returns `status=started` immediately. `business_automation.ingest` builds plan nodes that call `run_operation`, so an execution-plan node can be marked complete before Hooba has created the draft; the manifest may then skip an in-flight or failed row after a crash. Add a synchronous completion mode or durable run polling, and record progress only after a successful `DraftReceipt`.

suggestions.title: Keep workbook parsing off the event loop
suggestions.rationale: The existing async ingestion function calls `pandas.read_excel()` synchronously, and also performs synchronous filesystem reads and manifest writes. A BBVA parser will likely add more blocking workbook inspection. Put the complete parse/reconciliation operation behind `asyncio.to_thread()` or a dedicated worker boundary and test responsiveness under a large workbook.

suggestions.title: Add idempotency across header-plus-line draft creation
suggestions.rationale: The proposed invoice and purchase flows perform multiple POSTs, but the current generic request path has no idempotency key or transaction correlation. A failure after header creation and before lines can create an orphan draft, and retrying the composite can duplicate it; the existing statement manifest only tracks plan rows. Persist a client correlation key, reconcile existing drafts before retry, and disable unsafe transport retries for non-idempotent writes.

suggestions.title: Preserve the existing AEAT verdict contract and fail closed on uncertainty
suggestions.rationale: The auto-finance specification requires `DeductibilityVerdict` fields for `rule_id`, caps, invoice requirements, status, and cited legal basis, plus profile-dependent rules and review states. The proposed rule summary omits several of these semantics. Unknown categories, missing fiscal profile data, and ambiguous matches should produce `needs_review`/draft records with raw evidence, never a guessed deductible percentage.
